sample: The tracked file keeps 58,213 of the catalogue's 20,416,142 rows (packages/bake/authoring/nearby-universe/wisescos-sample.mts): of the 5,515,837 with photometric redshift 0.1 to 0.4, brighter than absolute R -21.5 and outside DESI's footprint (9,992 deg², found from the tracked DESI sample), those on the 20,409 deg² the catalogue covers well, thinned in each redshift bin 0.02 wide to the DESI sample's count per sky cell, by WISE id; with wiseID, RA, DEC, Z, R and the redshift bin C.
meaning: The WISE x SuperCOSMOS galaxies (Bilicki et al. 2016) where DESI did not look, from photometric redshift 0.1 to 0.4 and brighter than absolute R -21.5, at DESI's density in each redshift bin, each at its comoving distance in the Planck 2018 cosmology: they close DESI's two cones into one ball. Their photometric redshifts are about 15% uncertain, so they sit less sharply in depth than DESI's.

colorBy.basis: This catalogue has no g, r and z fluxes to colour a galaxy as DESI's are coloured. Each galaxy takes the median colour DESI's own galaxies show in its redshift bin (column 6, bins 0.02 wide from 0.1): each channel's median over the prepared DESI bank's colours, which wisescos-sample.mts prints. The colour says how galaxies at that distance look, not how this one does.

toneBy.basis: DESI's sample's tone scale (its recipe), so a fill galaxy is as bright as a DESI galaxy of the same absolute magnitude: its R magnitude at its Planck 2018 luminosity distance, full at -23.4 and 40% at -22.5. R is the photographic band nearest DESI's r; the two differ by a few tenths of a magnitude, and neither is k-corrected.
